$comment.0: The instruction-surface census as an anchor rather than a snapshot. Written by scripts/check-instruction-surface.js alone; scripts/resolve-ticket.js and the guard-issue-close core (scripts/lib/issue-close-host.js) also read it (#1876, #1913).
$comment.1: COUNTS are re-measured on every daily repo-checks run. VERDICTS are behavioural (mantahostels#886) and are re-measured only when the digest beside them moves. A guard's digest hashes its code with comments and layout dropped, so a comment-only edit moves none (#1876, scripts/lib/census-digest.js), and a shell guard's also hashes each docs/agents/rules/ file its code names, so a reworded rule moves it (#1914).
$comment.2: Re-anchoring with --rebaseline asserts that you re-measured what moved. Nothing checks that you did. --only <key>[,<key>...] (mantahostels#2105) narrows a re-anchor to named guards/poolFiles rel paths, hookCommands keys (spelt as below) and the `hooks` or `skills` count (#1879), leaving every other row reporting. A new guard's row is written by hand with an empty digest, then --only fills it.
$comment.3: Digests and pool bytes are anchored at the census's own tree (measuredAt.tree), not at the day this file was written: --rebaseline --at <rev>.
$comment.4: A verdict has two halves and both are recorded: `verdict` is timing (does it fire at the moment of need), `selfSufficient` is whether what it prints carries the rule.
$comment.5: guards holds every hook-wired script that prints rule text, plus check-roadmap-valid.js, a pre-commit checker that does, and check-weakens-line.js, a commit-msg one (#2235). name-issue-session.sh and clear-rule-latch.sh were measured and print no rule, so carry no verdict to anchor.
$comment.6: hookCommands anchors each hook entry's full live command text under the checker's buildHookKey: `<event> <scriptPath>`, plus ` if <cond>` where the entry has an `if` condition (#1604).
